title: Michigan's 11th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: An open seat race for Michigan's 11th Congressional District, which covers central Oakland County including Farmington Hills, Ferndale, Pontiac, and Troy. Incumbent Rep. Haley Stevens (D) is not seeking re-election and is instead running for the U.S. Senate, creating a competitive open seat contest. The Democratic primary field includes State Senate President Pro Tempore Jeremy Moss, former Ford Global Vehicle Engineering head Don Ufford, attorney and former prosecutor Aisha Farooqi, and Waterford School Board Trustee John Paul Torres. Troy Mayor Ethan Baker is running unopposed for the Republican nomination. The district, which voted for Joe Biden in 2020 and has been represented by Democrats since 2019, is expected to be a key battleground in the fight for control of the U.S. House.
polling_note: No public opinion polls specific to the MI-11 general election matchup were found as of mid-2026, given the primary has not yet occurred.

candidates.name: Ethan Baker
candidates.summary: Ethan Baker is the Mayor of Troy, Michigan, first elected in 2019 and re-elected in 2023. He serves on the Advisory Board of the U.S. Conference of Mayors and chairs the Great Lakes Fishery Commission. Baker announced his campaign for Michigan's 11th Congressional District in May 2026 and is running unopposed in the Republican primary.

candidates.name: Jeremy Moss
candidates.summary: Jeremy Moss is the Michigan State Senate President Pro Tempore, representing District 7 since 2023, having previously served in the state House and on the Southfield City Council. He was the first openly gay member of the Michigan Senate and has built a reputation as a prolific lawmaker who sponsored the most bills signed into law of any state legislator in 2023. Moss is running for the 11th Congressional District with endorsements from Governor Gretchen Whitmer and others, positioning himself as a tested leader with a record of legislative accomplishment.

candidates.summary: Aisha Farooqi is an attorney, former prosecutor, and the daughter of immigrants who was raised in Michigan. She has served as an Assistant Prosecuting Attorney in the Wayne County Prosecutor's Office and as a staff attorney at Lakeshore Legal Aid, and currently sits on the Michigan Child Abuse and Neglect Prevention Board. Farooqi is running for Congress in Michigan's 11th District to protect the American Dream and fight for working families.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polling exists as of mid-2026 (Democratic primary still pending). This forecast relies entirely on district fundamentals. MI-11 voted for Joe Biden in 2020 and has been represented by Democrats since 2019, suggesting a modest Democratic lean in central Oakland County. The open-seat nature eliminates incumbency advantage, keeping the race competitive. On the Democratic side, a competitive four-candidate primary means the eventual nominee will emerge from a contested race; frontrunner Jeremy Moss has strong endorsements (e.g., Gov. Whitmer) and legislative experience. Republicans are unified behind Troy Mayor Ethan Baker, a credible candidate running unopposed in the primary. However, the lack of any polling, uncertainty about which Democrat emerges and whether the primary is divisive, and the description of the district as a key House battleground all limit confidence. Lean Democratic is the most appropriate rating given the district's Democratic-leaning fundamentals, but confidence is low due to the absence of direct vote data.
